Sipho (an illustration) earns R20,000 a month, so all R240,000 of his yearly salary sits in the 18% tax step. Add a R20,000 bonus and his income for the year becomes R260,000. The first R5,100 of the bonus still fits in the 18% step, but the other R14,900 spills into the 26% step. Tax on the bonus: R918 + R3,874 = R4,792. So December's payslip shows about R6,900 in tax instead of the usual R2,100. It isn't a penalty: every extra rand is taxed at your top rate, never your average rate.

Full guide: "Your Bonus or 13th Cheque: How It's Taxed and What to Do With It (South Africa 2026)" on the Money From Zero channel.
